# SPI Master – Programmer's Model v0.3

General-purpose SPI master for flash, ADCs and sensors on the SoC peripheral bus.

## Features
- Supports SPI modes 0–3 (CPOL/CPHA).
- SCLK = f_clk / (2 × (DIV + 1)). DIV is 16 bits.
- Up to 4 chip selects, active low; only one active at a time.
- Transfer size 8, 16 or 32 bits; MSB-first or LSB-first.
- Full duplex: every transfer shifts out TXDATA and shifts in RXDATA.
- Optional "hold CS" so multi-word flash commands can stay in one CS window.
- Interrupt on transfer done.

## Bus
32-bit simple register bus: `addr[4:0]`, `wdata[31:0]`, `we`, `re`, `rdata[31:0]`. Reads
return data one cycle after `re`. No wait states.

## Register map

| Offset | Name | Access | Bits | Description |
|--------|------|--------|------|-------------|
| 0x00 | CTRL | RW | [0] EN | Block enable. |
| | | | [1] CPOL | Idle level of SCLK. |
| | | | [2] CPHA | 0 = sample on leading edge, 1 = sample on trailing edge. |
| | | | [3] LSB_FIRST | Bit order. |
| | | | [5:4] SIZE | 00 = 8 bit, 01 = 16 bit, 10 = 32 bit, 11 = reserved. |
| | | | [9:8] CS_SEL | Chip select used by the next transfer. |
| | | | [10] CS_HOLD | Keep CS asserted after the transfer. |
| | | | [16] IRQ_EN | Interrupt enable. |
| 0x04 | CLKDIV | RW | [15:0] DIV | SCLK divider. |
| 0x08 | TXDATA | WO | [31:0] | Writing starts a transfer. Data is right-aligned. |
| 0x0C | RXDATA | RO | [31:0] | Last received word, right-aligned. |
| 0x10 | STATUS | R/W1C | [0] BUSY (RO), [1] DONE (W1C), [2] TX_OVR (W1C) | TX_OVR = TXDATA written while busy. |

## Timing
- At least half an SCLK period from CS assertion to the first SCLK edge, and from the last
  SCLK edge to CS de-assertion.
- At least half an SCLK period of CS high between transfers.
- Up to 25 MHz SCLK with a 100 MHz system clock is required. Faster is a bonus.

# Micro-architecture: `spi_master`

## 1. Overview

`spi_master` is a memory-mapped, full-duplex SPI master. A write to TXDATA starts one
transfer of 8, 16 or 32 bits on the selected chip select, in any of the four CPOL/CPHA
modes, with configurable bit order. SCLK is generated from the system clock by a
half-period counter. All pin outputs (`sclk`, `mosi`, `cs_n`) come straight from flops.

Key features:
- One half-period engine: every SPI edge is an "event" generated when the divider counter expires; mode decoding decides whether an event drives MOSI or samples MISO.
- One shift register for TX and one for RX, with alignment muxes for size and bit order.
- Guaranteed half-SCLK CS lead, lag and minimum CS-high time.
- CS_HOLD for multi-word transactions; DONE interrupt with W1C status.

## 2. Interface

| Name | Dir | Width | Description |
|------|-----|-------|-------------|
| **Clock / reset** | | | |
| `clk` | in | 1 | System clock (100 MHz target). |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Active-low reset; async assert, sync de-assert. |
| **Register bus** | | | |
| `addr` | in | 5 | Byte address; bits [1:0] ignored. |
| `wdata` | in | 32 | Write data. |
| `we` | in | 1 | Write strobe (single cycle). |
| `re` | in | 1 | Read strobe (single cycle). |
| `rdata` | out | 32 | Read data, valid the cycle after `re` (registered). |
| **Interrupt** | | | |
| `irq` | out | 1 | Level interrupt: `IRQ_EN & DONE`. |
| **SPI pins** | | | |
| `sclk` | out | 1 | Serial clock (registered). |
| `mosi` | out | 1 | Master out, slave in (registered). |
| `miso` | in | 1 | Master in, slave out. |
| `cs_n` | out | `NUM_CS` | Active-low chip selects (registered, at most one low). |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Legal range | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `NUM_CS` | 4 | 1–4 | Number of chip-select outputs (`CS_SEL` values ≥ `NUM_CS` select none). |
| `DIV_W` | 16 | 1–16 | Divider width (CLKDIV[DIV_W-1:0] implemented). |

Derived: `half_period = DIV + 1` system clocks; `f_sclk = f_clk / (2 * (DIV + 1))`.
At 100 MHz, DIV = 1 gives 25 MHz and DIV = 0 gives 50 MHz.

## 4. Block Diagram

```
         addr/wdata/we/re
               |
        +--------------+   ctrl/div/cs_sel      +---------------------------+
        |  reg_if      |----------------------->|        spi_engine         |
        |  CTRL CLKDIV |   start, tx_word       |  +---------+  event,lead  |
        |  STATUS RX   |----------------------->|  | div_cnt |---------+    |
        |  rdata reg   |<-----------------------|  +---------+         v    |
        +--------------+  done, busy, rx_word   |  +---------+   +---------+|---> sclk
              |                                 |  |  FSM    |-->| edge    ||
             irq                                |  | IDLE/   |   | decode  ||---> mosi
                                                |  | XFER/   |   +---------+|
                                                |  | LAG/GAP |     |   |    |<--- miso
                                                |  +---------+  drive sample|
                                                |    tx_sh[32]  rx_sh[32]   |---> cs_n[NUM_CS]
                                                +---------------------------+
```

| Instance | Module | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `u_regs` | `spi_regs` | Register decode, CTRL/CLKDIV storage, STATUS W1C logic, read mux, `irq`. |
| `u_eng` | `spi_engine` | Divider, FSM, edge counter, shift registers, pin flops. |

## 5. Datapath

**Register block**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `ctrl_q` | 17 (bits 0–5, 8–10, 16 used) | 0 | CTRL fields. |
| `div_q` | `DIV_W` | 0 | CLKDIV. |
| `rx_q` | 32 | 0 | RXDATA, written by the engine on completion. |
| `done_q` | 1 | 0 | STATUS.DONE (sticky, W1C). |
| `txovr_q` | 1 | 0 | STATUS.TX_OVR (sticky, W1C). |
| `rdata_q` | 32 | 0 | Registered read data. |

`start = we && addr[4:2]==3'd2 && EN && !busy`; `txovr_set = we && addr[4:2]==3'd2 && busy`.

**Engine**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `state` | 2 | IDLE | FSM state. |
| `div_cnt` | `DIV_W` | 0 | Half-period counter; `event = (div_cnt == div_lat)`. |
| `edge_cnt` | 6 | 0 | SPI edge index 0..2N−1 (N ≤ 32 → 64 edges). |
| `tx_sh` | 32 | 0 | Transmit shift register. |
| `rx_sh` | 32 | 0 | Receive shift register. |
| `cfg_lat` | 7 | 0 | {CPOL, CPHA, LSB_FIRST, SIZE, CS_SEL} latched at `start`; `div_lat` too. |
| `sclk_q` | 1 | 0 (driven to CPOL in IDLE) | SCLK pin flop. |
| `mosi_q` | 1 | 0 | MOSI pin flop. |
| `cs_n_q` | `NUM_CS` | all 1 | CS pin flops. |
| `cs_held` | 1 | 0 | CS still asserted from a previous CS_HOLD transfer. |

**Size and bit-order alignment** (N = 8/16/32 from `SIZE`; `last_edge = 2N − 1`):

```verilog
// load (MSB-first left-aligns so the head is always tx_sh[31]; LSB-first keeps head at tx_sh[0])
tx_load = lsb ? tx_word
              : (size==2'd0) ? {tx_word[7:0], 24'b0}
              : (size==2'd1) ? {tx_word[15:0], 16'b0} : tx_word;
tx_head = lsb ? tx_sh[0] : tx_sh[31];
tx_next = lsb ? {1'b0, tx_sh[31:1]} : {tx_sh[30:0], 1'b0};

// sample: MSB-first fills from the bottom (ends right-aligned); LSB-first fills from the top
rx_next = lsb ? {miso, rx_sh[31:1]} : {rx_sh[30:0], miso};
rx_word = !lsb ? rx_sh
              : (size==2'd0) ? {24'b0, rx_sh[31:24]}
              : (size==2'd1) ? {16'b0, rx_sh[31:16]} : rx_sh;
```

For MSB-first transfers smaller than 32 bits, `rx_word` keeps stale upper bits from earlier
transfers unless `rx_sh` is cleared at `start`. It is cleared (`rx_sh <= 0` on load), so the
upper bits read 0.

**Edge decode** (per event in XFER; `lead = !edge_cnt[0]`):

| Mode | CPHA | Drive MOSI (`mosi_q<=tx_head; tx_sh<=tx_next`) | Sample MISO (`rx_sh<=rx_next`) |
|------|------|-----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 0, 2 | 0 | at `start` (first bit) and on trailing edges except the last | leading edges |
| 1, 3 | 1 | leading edges | trailing edges |

`sclk_q <= ~sclk_q` on every XFER event; in IDLE `sclk_q <= CPOL` (from `ctrl_q`, so idle
polarity follows the register immediately).

## 6. Control Logic

**FSM**

| State | Enc | Outputs | Transition |
|-------|-----|---------|------------|
| IDLE | 2'd0 | `busy=0`; `sclk_q=CPOL`; `cs_n` = held CS or all 1 | `start` → XFER: latch cfg/div, `tx_sh<=tx_load`, `rx_sh<=0`, `div_cnt<=0`, `edge_cnt<=0`, drive `cs_n_q[CS_SEL]=0`. If CPHA=0, also do a drive (`mosi_q<=tx_head(tx_load)`, shift). |
| XFER | 2'd1 | `busy=1` | On each `event`: toggle SCLK, perform drive/sample per table, `edge_cnt++`. When `event && edge_cnt==last_edge` → LAG, `rx_q<=rx_word` (one cycle later via `rx_wr` strobe). |
| LAG | 2'd2 | `busy=1`, CS still low | `event` → if `CS_HOLD` (live register value): IDLE, `cs_held<=1`, `done_set`; else `cs_n_q<=all 1`, → GAP. |
| GAP | 2'd3 | `busy=1`, CS high | `event` → IDLE, `done_set`. |

`div_cnt` behaviour: in XFER/LAG/GAP, `div_cnt <= event ? 0 : div_cnt + 1`; held at 0 in IDLE.

**Held chip select.** If a transfer starts while `cs_held=1` and `CS_SEL` names a different
CS than the held one, the held CS is released and the new one asserted in the same cycle.
The required CS-high gap does not apply between different devices. If `CS_HOLD` is cleared
while IDLE with `cs_held=1`, the engine de-asserts all CS on the next cycle (`cs_held<=0`).

**Status / interrupt**

```verilog
done_q   <= done_set | (done_q & ~(w1c_status & wdata[1]));
txovr_q  <= txovr_set | (txovr_q & ~(w1c_status & wdata[2]));   // set wins over clear
irq       = ctrl_q[16] & done_q;
busy      = (state != IDLE);
```

## 7. Timing & Pipeline

- **Transfer duration** (clocks, from the TXDATA write cycle to `DONE`): `1 + (2N + 2) × (DIV + 1)` with CS de-assertion, or `1 + (2N + 1) × (DIV + 1)` with CS_HOLD.
- **CS lead / lag / gap:** exactly one half-period each (meets the spec minimum).
- **Max SCLK:** 50 MHz at DIV = 0 (100 MHz clk). MISO is sampled on the system-clock edge that launches the sampling SCLK edge. The round trip (`sclk` out + slave tCO + `miso` in + setup) must fit in one half-period: 10 ns at DIV = 0, 20 ns at DIV = 1. 25 MHz is the guaranteed spec point.
- **Throughput:** with back-to-back writes polling BUSY, 8-bit at DIV = 1: 1 + 18 × 2 = 37 clocks per byte, i.e. about 21.6 Mbit/s.

Mode 0, 8-bit MSB-first, `TXDATA = 0xA5` (1010_0101), DIV = 0. Values are those seen during each cycle:

| Cycle | State | edge_cnt | Event | `cs_n` | `sclk` | `mosi` | Action at end of cycle |
|-------|-------|----------|-------|--------|--------|--------|------------------------|
| 0 | IDLE | – | – | 1 | 0 | x | TXDATA write → start, drive b7 |
| 1 | XFER | 0 | lead ↑ | 0 | 0 | 1 (b7) | sample MISO b7 |
| 2 | XFER | 1 | trail ↓ | 0 | 1 | 1 | drive b6 |
| 3 | XFER | 2 | lead ↑ | 0 | 0 | 0 (b6) | sample b6 |
| 4 | XFER | 3 | trail ↓ | 0 | 1 | 0 | drive b5 |
| … | … | … | … | 0 | … | … | … |
| 15 | XFER | 14 | lead ↑ | 0 | 0 | 1 (b0) | sample b0 |
| 16 | XFER | 15 | trail ↓ | 0 | 1 | 1 | last edge, no drive; → LAG, capture RX |
| 17 | LAG | – | event | 0 | 0 | 1 | release CS → GAP |
| 18 | GAP | – | event | 1 | 0 | 1 | → IDLE, DONE=1 |
| 19 | IDLE | – | – | 1 | 0 | 1 | `irq` high if IRQ_EN |

## 8. Clocking & Reset

- **One clock domain.** SCLK is a data output toggled by a flop, never a clock inside the block, so there are no generated-clock constraints internally. Constrain `sclk`/`mosi`/`cs_n` as outputs and `miso` as an input relative to a virtual clock derived from `clk / (2 × (DIV + 1))`, or use a multicycle path for low speeds.
- **MISO is not double-synchronized.** It is source-synchronous to our own SCLK, so a 2-flop synchronizer would only add latency and break sampling at high speed. Use an IOB input flop.
- **Reset:** all registers clear; `cs_n_q` resets to all ones (no device selected). `sclk_q` resets to 0 and follows CPOL from the first IDLE cycle; with CPOL = 1, firmware should set CTRL before selecting a device.
- **Configuration:** CPOL/CPHA/SIZE/LSB/CS_SEL/DIV are latched at `start`, so writes to CTRL/CLKDIV during a transfer only affect the next transfer. Exceptions: CS_HOLD is read live at the end of LAG, and CPOL drives idle SCLK directly.

## 9. Corner Cases & Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| TXDATA write while BUSY | Ignored; TX_OVR set. |
| TXDATA write while EN=0 | Ignored, no flag (block disabled). |
| SIZE = 2'b11 (reserved) | Treated as 32-bit. |
| CS_SEL ≥ NUM_CS | Transfer runs with no CS asserted (useful for dummy clocks); documented, not an error. |
| CPOL changed while `cs_held` | SCLK moves to the new idle level while CS is low, which the slave sees as a clock edge. Firmware must not do this; flagged by an assertion. |
| EN cleared during a transfer | Current transfer completes (EN only gates `start`). |
| W1C clear of DONE in the same cycle as `done_set` | Set wins, so no completion event is lost. |
| RXDATA read during transfer | Returns the previous word (`rx_q` is updated only at completion). |

## 10. Verification Plan

**Testbench:** register-level driver plus an SPI slave BFM for each mode. The BFM checks
CS-to-SCLK lead/lag/gap, samples MOSI on the correct edge, and returns a scripted MISO
pattern with configurable tCO. A scoreboard checks RXDATA and the MOSI bit stream.

**Directed tests**
1. Reset: all `cs_n` high, `sclk` 0, BUSY 0.
2. For each mode (0–3) × SIZE (8/16/32) × order (MSB/LSB): 0xA5A5_5A5A pattern, walking-1, all-0, all-1.
3. DIV sweep {0, 1, 2, 7, 0xFFFF}: measure SCLK period = 2 × (DIV + 1) clocks.
4. CS lead/lag/gap = DIV + 1 clocks each.
5. CS_HOLD: 3 transfers in one CS window, then clear CS_HOLD → CS releases.
6. CS switch while held → old CS high and new CS low in the same cycle.
7. TX_OVR: write during transfer, check flag and that the transfer is unaffected.
8. DONE/irq: W1C clearing, simultaneous set/clear.

**Random tests:** random config per transfer, random DIV in 0..15, random MISO data and
slave tCO up to 0.8 × half-period; 5k transfers.

**Assertions (SVA)**

```systemverilog
a_cs_onehot0:  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) $onehot0(~cs_n));
a_sclk_idle:   assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) state==IDLE && !cs_held |-> sclk==ctrl_q[1]);
a_sclk_cs:     assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) $changed(sclk) |-> $past(state)==XFER || $past(state)==IDLE);
a_edges:       // number of sclk toggles between cs_n fall and rise == 2N (checked in monitor)
a_no_cpol_chg: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) cs_held |-> $stable(ctrl_q[1]));
a_busy_start:  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) start |=> busy);
```

**Coverage:** mode × size × order cross (24 bins); DIV ∈ {0, 1, small, large}; CS_HOLD
chains of length 1, 2, ≥ 3; every CS_SEL value including out-of-range; TX_OVR; DONE
set/clear collision.

## 11. Assumptions & Open Questions

1. **CPHA definition:** CPHA = 0 drives the first bit before the first edge and samples on leading edges; CPHA = 1 drives on leading edges and samples on trailing edges (standard Motorola convention).
2. **MISO sample point** is the exact SCLK edge (zero delay). For higher speeds or long traces, a future `SAMPLE_DLY` field could sample 1–2 system clocks later; not required for 25 MHz.
3. **No TX/RX FIFO.** The spec defines single TXDATA/RXDATA registers. DMA or FIFOs can be added at the register layer.
4. **CS_HOLD is evaluated at the end of LAG**, so firmware can clear it during the last transfer of a burst and get automatic release.
5. **MOSI holds the last bit** between transfers (no forced idle level). The spec does not define an idle level.
6. **Reserved SIZE = 11 behaves as 32-bit** rather than raising an error.
7. **Reads have no side effects** (RXDATA read does not clear DONE); confirm with the driver team.

# Micro-architecture: `i2c_master`

## 1. Overview

`i2c_master` is a firmware-driven, byte-level I2C master for Standard mode (100 kHz) and
Fast mode (≤ 400 kHz) with open-drain SCL/SDA. Firmware writes one command per byte (any
mix of START, WRITE, READ, ACK value and STOP) and gets an interrupt when it finishes.

The design has two layers:
- **Byte controller** – decodes the command register and sequences START → 8 data bits → ACK bit → STOP.
- **Bit controller** – runs each bit-level primitive (START, STOP, WRITE-bit, READ-bit) as a series of quarter-period phases, drives the open-drain enables, honours clock stretching, and detects arbitration loss.

Key features:
- Repeated START (Sr) for EEPROM random reads.
- 7-bit addressing: firmware sends the address byte `{addr[6:0], R/W}` with a START|WRITE command. No dedicated address hardware is needed.
- Clock stretching and multi-master clock synchronization through SCL read-back.
- Arbitration-loss detection on SDA mismatch and on an unexpected STOP.
- Bus-busy tracking from START/STOP conditions on the bus.
- 2-flop synchronizers plus a programmable spike filter (≥ 50 ns) on SCL/SDA inputs.

## 2. Interface

| Name | Dir | Width | Description |
|------|-----|-------|-------------|
| **Clock / reset** | | | |
| `clk` | in | 1 | Peripheral clock (48 MHz nominal). |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Active-low reset; async assert, sync de-assert. |
| **Register bus** | | | |
| `addr` | in | 5 | Byte address; [1:0] ignored. |
| `wdata` | in | 32 | Write data. |
| `we` | in | 1 | Write strobe. |
| `re` | in | 1 | Read strobe. |
| `rdata` | out | 32 | Read data, registered, valid one cycle after `re`. |
| `irq` | out | 1 | `IEN & IF`. |
| **Pads (open drain)** | | | |
| `scl_i` | in | 1 | SCL pad input (asynchronous). |
| `scl_oe` | out | 1 | 1 = drive SCL low, 0 = release (pulled up externally). |
| `sda_i` | in | 1 | SDA pad input (asynchronous). |
| `sda_oe` | out | 1 | 1 = drive SDA low, 0 = release. |

Pad wrapper: `assign SCL = scl_oe ? 1'b0 : 1'bz; assign scl_i = SCL;` (same for SDA). The
block never drives a 1.

**Register map**

| Offset | Name | Access | Fields |
|--------|------|--------|--------|
| 0x00 | PRESC | RW | [15:0] quarter-period = PRESC + 1 clocks |
| 0x04 | CTRL | RW | [0] EN, [1] IEN, [6:4] FILT (spike-filter length, clocks) |
| 0x08 | TXR | RW | [7:0] byte to transmit |
| 0x0C | RXR | RO | [7:0] last byte received |
| 0x10 | CMD | WO | [0] STA, [1] STO, [2] RD, [3] WR, [4] ACK (value sent after a read: 0 = ACK, 1 = NACK), [7] IACK (clear IF) |
| 0x14 | STATUS | RO | [0] IF, [1] TIP, [2] AL, [3] BUSY (bus), [4] RXACK (1 = slave NACKed) |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Legal range | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `FILT_RST` | 3 | 0–7 | Reset value of CTRL.FILT. |

Recommended PRESC values (f_clk = 48 MHz):

| Mode | PRESC | Quarter `q` | SCL freq (no stretching) | tLOW / tHIGH |
|------|-------|-------------|--------------------------|--------------|
| Standard | 119 | 2.50 µs | 100 kHz | 5.0 / 5.0 µs (min 4.7 / 4.0) |
| Fast | 31 | 0.667 µs | 375 kHz | 1.33 / 1.33 µs (min 1.3 / 0.6) |

A 50 % duty cycle at exactly 400 kHz gives tLOW = 1.25 µs, which breaks the Fast-mode
minimum of 1.3 µs. 375 kHz is therefore the fastest compliant setting with this phase scheme
(see §11).

## 4. Block Diagram

```

 ---->| i2c_regs |--------->|  byte_ctrl FSM  |----------------->|  bit_ctrl FSM    |  sda_oe ---> SDA pad

 irq  | CTRL TXR |  done,   |                 | bit_done,dout,al |  owned           |

      +----------+  al, rxr                                        ^   ^       ^
                                                                   |   |       | start_det/stop_det
                                                           scl_f   |   | sda_f |
                                                       +-----------+---+-------+--+
                                       scl_i, sda_i -->| sync_2ff x2 + spike_filt |
                                                       |  + bus_busy detector     |
                                                       +--------------------------+
```

| Instance | Module | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `u_regs` | `i2c_regs` | Register file, CMD decode, IF/AL/TIP status, `irq`. |
| `u_byte` | `i2c_byte_ctrl` | Command sequencer and data shift register. |
| `u_bit` | `i2c_bit_ctrl` | Quarter-phase generator, pad enables, stretching, arbitration. |
| `u_in_scl`, `u_in_sda` | `i2c_in_filt` | 2-FF synchronizer + stability filter (`FILT` clocks). |
| `u_busmon` | `i2c_bus_mon` | START/STOP condition detection, `bus_busy`. |

## 5. Datapath

**Input conditioning (per line)**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `s_meta`, `s_sync` | 1 each | 1 | 2-FF synchronizer (lines idle high). |
| `f_cnt` | 3 | 0 | Counts consecutive clocks where `s_sync != filt`. |
| `filt` (`scl_f`/`sda_f`) | 1 | 1 | Filtered level; toggles when `f_cnt == FILT`. |

```verilog
if (s_sync == filt) f_cnt <= 0;
else if (f_cnt == filt_len) begin filt <= s_sync; f_cnt <= 0; end
else f_cnt <= f_cnt + 1;
```

With FILT = 3 at 48 MHz, a level must hold 4 clocks (83 ns) to be accepted, so 50 ns
spikes are rejected. Total input delay is 2 (sync) + 4 = 6 clocks (125 ns).

**Bus monitor:** `start_det = scl_f && sda_f_q && !sda_f`; `stop_det = scl_f && !sda_f_q && sda_f`
(`sda_f_q` is `sda_f` delayed one clock). `bus_busy` is set by `start_det` and cleared by `stop_det` (reset 0).

**Bit controller**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `q_cnt` | 16 | 0 | Quarter-period counter; `q_end = (q_cnt == presc)`. |
| `phase` | 3 | 0 | Phase index within the current primitive (P1..P6 → 0..5). |
| `bstate` | 2 | B_IDLE | Primitive being executed: B_IDLE / B_START / B_STOP / B_DATA. |
| `din_q` | 1 | 1 | Bit to drive for B_DATA (1 = release). |
| `dout_q` | 1 | 1 | SDA sampled at the end of P3. |
| `scl_oe_q`, `sda_oe_q` | 1 each | 0 | Pad enables (registered). |
| `owned` | 1 | 0 | This master owns the bus (between its START and STOP). |
| `al_q` | 1 | 0 | Arbitration-lost pulse to the byte controller. |

**Byte controller**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `cstate` | 3 | C_IDLE | Byte-controller state. |
| `cmd_q` | 5 | 0 | Latched {ACK, WR, RD, STO, STA}; bits cleared as each part completes. |
| `sh` | 8 | 0 | Shift register (loaded from TXR on WRITE, collects bits on READ). |
| `bitcnt` | 3 | 0 | Data bit counter (7 → 0). |
| `rxr_q` | 8 | 0 | RXR. |
| `rxack_q` | 1 | 0 | ACK bit sampled after a WRITE (1 = NACK). |
| `tip_q`, `if_q`, `al_s` | 1 each | 0 | STATUS bits. |

## 6. Control Logic

**Bit-level primitives.** Every phase lasts `q = PRESC + 1` clocks. Phases marked **W**
release SCL and do not start counting until `scl_f == 1`; that is how clock stretching and
multi-master clock synchronization are handled.

| Primitive | P1 | P2 | P3 (W) | P4 | P5 | P6 |
|-----------|----|----|--------|----|----|----|
| START (bus owned → Sr) | SCL 0, SDA hold | SCL 0, SDA 1 | SCL 1, SDA 1 | SCL 1, SDA 1 | SCL 1, **SDA 0** | SCL 1, SDA 0 |
| START (bus idle) | – skip | – skip | SCL 1, SDA 1 | SCL 1, SDA 1 | SCL 1, **SDA 0** | SCL 1, SDA 0 |
| DATA (write/read bit) | SCL 0, SDA hold | SCL 0, SDA = `din` | SCL 1, SDA = `din`; **sample at end** | SCL 1, SDA = `din` | – | – |
| STOP | SCL 0, SDA hold | SCL 0, SDA 0 | SCL 1, SDA 0 | SCL 1, SDA 0 | SCL 1, **SDA 1** | SCL 1, SDA 1; check |

"SCL 1/SDA 1" means the enable is released (`oe = 0`). A READ bit is a DATA primitive with
`din = 1`. The ACK bit is a DATA primitive with `din = ACK` (after a read) or `din = 1` (after
a write, sampling the slave's ACK).

**Bit-controller transitions**

| Event | Action |
|-------|--------|
| `bit_cmd` issued in B_IDLE | Go to the primitive; `phase` = P1 (or P3 for START with `!owned`). |
| `q_end` in a non-W phase, or in a W phase after `scl_f` went high | `phase++`; `q_cnt <= 0`. |
| End of last phase | `bit_done` pulse; B_IDLE. START sets `owned=1`, STOP clears it. |
| P4 of DATA and `scl_f == 0` (another master pulled SCL low) | End P4 early (clock synchronization): `bit_done` now; the next P1 continues low. |

**Arbitration loss (`al`)**, raised for one clock:

```verilog
al = (bstate==B_DATA  && phase==P3 && q_end && scl_f && din_q && !sda_f)   // we sent 1, bus shows 0
   | (bstate==B_START && phase==P4 && q_end && !sda_f)                     // SDA held low by someone else
   | (bstate==B_STOP  && phase==P6 && q_end && !sda_f)                     // could not release SDA
   | (stop_det && owned && bstate!=B_STOP);                                // foreign STOP
```

On `al`: `scl_oe_q <= 0`, `sda_oe_q <= 0`, `owned <= 0`, and the bit controller returns to B_IDLE.

**Byte-controller FSM**

| State | Enc | Action | Next |
|-------|-----|--------|------|
| C_IDLE | 3'd0 | Wait for a CMD write with any of STA/WR/RD/STO set (and EN). Latch `cmd_q`, set TIP. | STA → C_START (only when `!bus_busy || owned`; else wait here); WR → C_WRITE (`sh<=TXR`, `bitcnt<=7`); RD → C_READ (`bitcnt<=7`); STO → C_STOP. |
| C_START | 3'd1 | Issue START; wait `bit_done`. | WR → C_WRITE; RD → C_READ; STO → C_STOP; else C_DONE. |
| C_WRITE | 3'd2 | Issue DATA with `din=sh[7]`; on `bit_done`: `sh<<=1`, `bitcnt--`. | After bit 0 → C_ACK. |
| C_READ | 3'd3 | Issue DATA with `din=1`; on `bit_done`: `sh<={sh[6:0],dout}`. | After bit 0 → C_ACK. |
| C_ACK | 3'd4 | Issue DATA with `din = WR ? 1 : cmd_q.ACK`; on `bit_done`: WR → `rxack_q<=dout`; RD → `rxr_q<=sh`. | STO → C_STOP; else C_DONE. |
| C_STOP | 3'd5 | Issue STOP; wait `bit_done`. | C_DONE. |
| C_DONE | 3'd6 | `tip<=0`, `if<=1`, clear `cmd_q`. | C_IDLE. |

Any state with `al` → `al_s<=1`, `if<=1`, `tip<=0`, clear `cmd_q`, C_IDLE.

Status equations: `if_q` is cleared by CMD.IACK (set wins); `al_s` is cleared by the next CMD
write that has STA set; `irq = IEN & if_q`.

## 7. Timing & Pipeline

- **Primitive durations:** DATA = 4q; START = 4q from idle, 6q for Sr; STOP = 6q. Stretching adds the time spent waiting in a W phase.
- **Byte time:** 9 bits × 4q = 36q (90 µs at Standard mode, 24 µs at Fast mode / PRESC = 31).
- **Firmware gap:** between commands SCL stays released (high) with SDA unchanged, so the bus is idle-safe while firmware services `irq`.
- **Spec timing (Standard, q = 2.5 µs):** tSU;DAT = 1q = 2.5 µs (min 0.25), tVD;DAT = 1q ≤ 3.45 µs, tSU;STA = tHD;STA = tSU;STO = 2q = 5 µs, tBUF ≥ 4q.
- **Spec timing (Fast, q = 0.667 µs):** tVD;DAT = 0.667 µs ≤ 0.9 µs; all other minima met at 2q = 1.33 µs.

Phase-level trace: command `STA|WR` with `TXR = 0xA0` (address 0x50, write) on an idle bus, slave ACKs, no stretching:

| Quarter | Primitive / phase | SCL | SDA | Note |
|---------|-------------------|-----|-----|------|
| 0 | START P3 | 1 | 1 | |
| 1 | START P4 | 1 | 1 | SDA checked high at end |
| 2 | START P5 | 1 | 0 | **START condition** |
| 3 | START P6 | 1 | 0 | `owned=1` at end |
| 4 | b7 P1 | 0 | 0 | SCL falls, SDA held |
| 5 | b7 P2 | 0 | 1 | b7 = 1 (released) |
| 6 | b7 P3 | 1 | 1 | sample: 1 → no AL |
| 7 | b7 P4 | 1 | 1 | |
| 8 | b6 P1 | 0 | 1 | |
| 9 | b6 P2 | 0 | 0 | b6 = 0 |
| 10–11 | b6 P3–P4 | 1 | 0 | |
| 12–35 | b5..b0 | … | 1,0,0,0,0,0 | same 4-phase pattern |
| 36 | ACK P1 | 0 | 0 | |
| 37 | ACK P2 | 0 | 0 | master releases, slave drives 0 |
| 38 | ACK P3 | 1 | 0 | `dout=0` → RXACK = 0 |
| 39 | ACK P4 | 1 | 0 | `bit_done` → C_DONE, IF = 1 |

Total: 40q = 4800 clocks (100 µs) in Standard mode.

EEPROM random read = 4 commands: `STA|WR (A0)` → `WR (addr_hi)` → `WR (addr_lo)` →
`STA|WR (A1)` [Sr] → `RD|ACK=1|STO`.

## 8. Clocking & Reset

- **Single clock domain** (`clk`). `scl_i`/`sda_i` are asynchronous and pass through 2-FF synchronizers (`ASYNC_REG`) before the filter. No other CDC.
- SCL is generated as a data signal (open-drain enable), not as a clock.
- **Reset:** all FSMs idle, both pad enables released (lines float high), `owned=0`, `bus_busy=0`, filters preset to 1.
- **EN = 0:** pad enables are forced to 0 and the FSMs held idle; register writes are still accepted.
- **PRESC/FILT changes** take effect immediately; firmware must only change them while `TIP=0`.

## 9. Corner Cases & Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| Slave NACKs address or data | RXACK=1 reported; transaction not aborted automatically; firmware issues STO. |
| Clock stretching (slave holds SCL low) | W phase waits indefinitely for `scl_f==1` (see §11 on timeouts). |
| Another master wins arbitration | `al`: lines released immediately, AL=1, IF=1. The rest of the current byte is not clocked; the winning master continues undisturbed. |
| STA while another master owns the bus (`bus_busy && !owned`) | Command waits in C_IDLE (TIP=1) until `stop_det`, then starts. |
| Foreign STOP while we own the bus | Treated as arbitration loss. |
| CMD written while TIP=1 | Ignored (no queueing); firmware must wait for IF. |
| CMD with STA and STO only | START immediately followed by STOP (bus reset pattern) – legal. |
| CMD with RD and WR both set | WR takes precedence; RD ignored. |
| Spike < FILT+1 clocks on SCL/SDA | Filtered; no state change. |
| Reset in the middle of a transfer | Lines released; slaves may be left mid-byte (see §11, bus recovery). |

## 10. Verification Plan

**Testbench:** open-drain bus model (wired-AND with pull-up, configurable rise time). Agents:
an I2C slave model (24C256 behavioural EEPROM with ACK/NACK and clock stretching), a second
I2C master model to provoke arbitration, and a glitch injector.

**Directed tests**
1. Write byte to EEPROM: START, address, 2 addr bytes, data, STOP; check the EEPROM model contents.
2. Random read with repeated START and NACK on last byte.
3. Address NACK (no slave at address) → RXACK=1, then STOP.
4. Clock stretching of 0, 1q, 10q and 1 ms on a data bit and on ACK.
5. Arbitration: both masters address different slaves; the loser sees AL at the first differing bit, and the winner's transfer completes intact.
6. Foreign STOP during our transfer → AL.
7. STA while bus busy → waits for STOP, then proceeds.
8. Glitch injection of 1–5 clocks on SCL high and SDA during data → no corruption with FILT=3.
9. Standard and Fast PRESC: measure tLOW, tHIGH, tSU;STA, tHD;STA, tSU;STO, tBUF and tSU;DAT against I2C spec limits in the bus monitor.

**Random tests:** random command sequences (legal and illegal combinations), random stretching,
random arbitration start time, 2k transactions.

**Assertions (SVA)**

```systemverilog
a_no_start_in_data: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n)
                      bstate==B_DATA && phase inside {P3,P4} |-> $stable(sda_oe_q));
a_release_on_al:    assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) al |=> !scl_oe_q && !sda_oe_q);
a_owned_only_ours:  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) owned |-> bus_busy);
a_tip_if:           assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) $fell(tip_q) |-> if_q);
a_sda_changes_low:  // SDA output changes only while SCL output is low, except in START P5 / STOP P5
```

**Coverage:** every byte-controller transition; START from idle and Sr; ACK and NACK in
both directions; stretching in each W phase; arbitration loss in START, DATA (address and
data byte) and STOP; FILT values 0 and 7; Standard and Fast mode.

## 11. Assumptions & Open Questions

The spec left several items TBD. Decisions taken:

1. **CPU interface:** a register interface like the industry-standard OpenCores I2C (PRESC/CTRL/TXR/RXR/CMD/STATUS), one command per byte with an IF interrupt, chosen as "simple, byte-by-byte". It is on the same simple 32-bit bus as the other peripherals.
2. **Clock:** 48 MHz assumed; PRESC makes the design work with any f_clk ≥ 10 MHz. Below that, the 6-clock input delay becomes a significant part of q.
3. **Fast mode runs at 375 kHz**, not 400 kHz, to meet tLOW ≥ 1.3 µs with a 50 % duty cycle. An asymmetric low/high split (e.g. 3:2 phases) would allow 400 kHz; deferred.
4. **Input filtering:** "maybe filter inputs" is implemented as a programmable 0–7 clock stability filter, default 3 (rejects ≥ 50 ns spikes as required for Fast mode).
5. **No timeouts.** A slave stretching forever or a stuck bus blocks TIP. Recommend adding an SMBus-style 25–35 ms timeout and a 9-clock bus-recovery command in a later revision.
6. **NACK handling** is left to firmware (no automatic STOP).
7. **Bus-busy at reset** is assumed false; if another master is mid-transfer at our reset, the first STA could collide, which is then caught by arbitration detection.
8. **10-bit addressing, high-speed mode and slave mode** are out of scope.

# Micro-architecture: `async_fifo`

## 1. Overview

`async_fifo` moves 26-bit pixel words from the sensor clock domain (`wclk`, 74.25 MHz,
may stop) to the system clock domain (`rclk`, 200 MHz). The two clocks are fully
asynchronous. The design follows the classic Gray-pointer architecture:

- Each side keeps a binary pointer (for addressing and level arithmetic) and a registered Gray copy of it. Only the Gray copy crosses domains.
- A 2-FF synchronizer brings the Gray pointer into the other domain. Exactly one bit changes per increment, so a sample is always either the old or the new pointer, never a mix.
- `full` is computed only in the write domain and `empty` only in the read domain, from the local pointer and the synchronized remote pointer. Both are **pessimistic**: they may assert too early or de-assert too late, but data is never lost or duplicated.
- `almost_full` / `almost_empty` use the same synchronized pointers converted back to binary.
- Read data is registered: `rd_data` is valid the cycle after an accepted `rd_en`.
- Each side's reset also resets the other side, so the two pointers can never disagree after a one-sided reset.

## 2. Interface

| Name | Dir | Width | Description |
|------|-----|-------|-------------|
| **Write domain** | | | |
| `wclk` | in | 1 | Write clock (sensor pixel clock, 74.25 MHz, may stop). |
| `wrst_n` | in | 1 | Write-side reset, active low, asynchronous. |
| `wr_en` | in | 1 | Write request; accepted when `!wr_full`. |
| `wr_data` | in | `DATA_W` | `{sof, eol, rgb[23:0]}` (format is opaque to the FIFO). |
| `wr_full` | out | 1 | FIFO full (as seen from the write domain). |
| `wr_almost_full` | out | 1 | Write-side level ≥ `AF_LEVEL`. |
| **Read domain** | | | |
| `rclk` | in | 1 | Read clock (200 MHz). |
| `rrst_n` | in | 1 | Read-side reset, active low, asynchronous. |
| `rd_en` | in | 1 | Read request; accepted when `!rd_empty`. |
| `rd_data` | out | `DATA_W` | Read data, registered; valid in the cycle after an accepted read. |
| `rd_valid` | out | 1 | High for one cycle when `rd_data` holds newly read data (convenience). |
| `rd_empty` | out | 1 | FIFO empty (as seen from the read domain). |
| `rd_almost_empty` | out | 1 | Read-side level ≤ `AE_LEVEL`. |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Legal range | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `DATA_W` | 26 | 1–512 | Word width. |
| `DEPTH` | 32 | 4–4096, power of 2 | Number of entries. |
| `AF_LEVEL` | `DEPTH-4` | 1..`DEPTH` | `wr_almost_full` threshold. |
| `AE_LEVEL` | 4 | 0..`DEPTH-1` | `rd_almost_empty` threshold. |
| `SYNC_STAGES` | 2 | 2–4 | Synchronizer depth (3 recommended above ~500 MHz). |
| `ADDR_W` | `$clog2(DEPTH)` | derived | RAM address width (5). |
| `PTR_W` | `ADDR_W+1` | derived | Pointer width with wrap bit (6). |

## 4. Block Diagram

```
          wclk domain                          |                     rclk domain
                                               |
 wr_en ->+------------+ waddr  +-----------------------------+ raddr +------------+<- rd_en
 wr_data |  wptr_full |------->|  u_mem  DEPTH x DATA_W      |<------| rptr_empty |
         |  wbin,wgray|  we    |  write: wclk (sync)         |       | rbin,rgray |
         |  wfull,waf |------->|  read : async, into rd_data |       | rempty,rae |
         +------------+        +-------------+---------------+       +------------+
            |    ^                           |  rd_data_q (rclk)        |    ^
     wgray  |    | wq2_rgray                 v                    rgray |    | rq2_wgray
            |    |                       rd_data                        |    |
            |  +------------+                              +------------+    |
            |  | sync_r2w   |<---------------------------- | (rgray)    |    |
            |  | 2FF x PTR_W|                              +------------+    |
            |  +------------+                                               |
            |                                              +------------+   |
            +--------------------------------------------->| sync_w2r   |---+
                                                           | 2FF x PTR_W|
                                                           +------------+
   wrst_n --+--> [rst_sync wclk] --> wrst_int_n      rrst_n --+--> [rst_sync rclk] --> rrst_int_n
            |          ^ async clear = wrst_n & rrst_n          |          ^ async clear = wrst_n & rrst_n
            +----------------------------------------------------+
```

| Instance | Module | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `u_wptr` | `afifo_wptr_full` | Write pointers, `wr_full`, `wr_almost_full`. |
| `u_rptr` | `afifo_rptr_empty` | Read pointers, `rd_empty`, `rd_almost_empty`, `rd_data` register. |
| `u_mem` | `afifo_mem` | Dual-clock storage (LUT-RAM/flop array; BRAM for large DEPTH). |
| `u_sync_w2r` | `sync_ff #(PTR_W, SYNC_STAGES)` | `wgray` → `rq2_wgray` in `rclk`. |
| `u_sync_r2w` | `sync_ff #(PTR_W, SYNC_STAGES)` | `rgray` → `wq2_rgray` in `wclk`. |
| `u_wrst`, `u_rrst` | `rst_sync` | Reset synchronizers (async assert, sync release). |

## 5. Datapath

**Write domain registers** (`wclk`, reset by `wrst_int_n`)

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `wbin` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Binary write pointer; `waddr = wbin[ADDR_W-1:0]`. |
| `wgray` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Registered Gray of `wbin` (only signal crossing to `rclk`). |
| `wq1_rgray`, `wq2_rgray` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Synchronizer stages for `rgray`. |
| `wfull_q` | 1 | 0 | `wr_full`. |
| `waf_q` | 1 | 0 | `wr_almost_full`. |

```verilog
wire             w_fire     = wr_en & ~wfull_q;
wire [PTR_W-1:0] wbin_n     = wbin + w_fire;
wire [PTR_W-1:0] wgray_n    = (wbin_n >> 1) ^ wbin_n;
// full: next write Gray equals synced read Gray with the two MSBs inverted
wire             wfull_n    = (wgray_n == {~wq2_rgray[PTR_W-1:PTR_W-2], wq2_rgray[PTR_W-3:0]});
wire [PTR_W-1:0] wq2_rbin   = gray2bin(wq2_rgray);           // XOR prefix chain
wire [PTR_W-1:0] wlevel_n   = wbin_n - wq2_rbin;              // modulo 2^PTR_W, 0..DEPTH
wire             waf_n      = (wlevel_n >= AF_LEVEL);
```

**Read domain registers** (`rclk`, reset by `rrst_int_n`)

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `rbin` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Binary read pointer; `raddr = rbin[ADDR_W-1:0]`. |
| `rgray` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Registered Gray of `rbin`. |
| `rq1_wgray`, `rq2_wgray` | `PTR_W` | 0 | Synchronizer stages for `wgray`. |
| `rempty_q` | 1 | 1 | `rd_empty`. |
| `rae_q` | 1 | 1 | `rd_almost_empty`. |
| `rd_data_q` | `DATA_W` | 0 | Registered read data. |
| `rd_valid_q` | 1 | 0 | `rd_valid`. |

```verilog
wire             r_fire   = rd_en & ~rempty_q;
wire [PTR_W-1:0] rbin_n   = rbin + r_fire;
wire [PTR_W-1:0] rgray_n  = (rbin_n >> 1) ^ rbin_n;
wire             rempty_n = (rgray_n == rq2_wgray);
wire [PTR_W-1:0] rlevel_n = gray2bin(rq2_wgray) - rbin_n;
wire             rae_n    = (rlevel_n <= AE_LEVEL);
always @(posedge rclk) if (r_fire) rd_data_q <= mem[rbin[ADDR_W-1:0]];
```

**Memory:** `mem[0:DEPTH-1]`, `DATA_W` bits per entry. Synchronous write on `wclk` when
`w_fire`; asynchronous read addressed by `rbin` and captured into `rd_data_q` on `rclk`. Not
reset. At 32 × 26 bits this maps to dual-clock distributed RAM (FPGA) or an 832-flop array
(ASIC). For DEPTH ≥ 256, use a true dual-clock RAM macro with a synchronous read port; the
read-side timing is unchanged, because the RAM output register takes the place of `rd_data_q`.

## 6. Control Logic

There is no explicit FSM; each side is a pointer counter plus a registered flag comparator.

| Write-side condition | `wr_full` | Write accepted |
|----------------------|-----------|----------------|
| `wlevel < DEPTH` (as seen) | 0 | yes |
| `wlevel == DEPTH` (as seen) | 1 | no; `wr_en` ignored |

| Read-side condition | `rd_empty` | Read accepted |
|---------------------|------------|---------------|
| `rgray == rq2_wgray` | 1 | no; `rd_en` ignored |
| otherwise | 0 | yes; `rd_data` valid next cycle |

Gray conversion (`PTR_W = 6`):

```verilog
function [PTR_W-1:0] gray2bin(input [PTR_W-1:0] g);
  integer i; begin
    gray2bin[PTR_W-1] = g[PTR_W-1];
    for (i = PTR_W-2; i >= 0; i = i-1) gray2bin[i] = gray2bin[i+1] ^ g[i];
  end
endfunction
```

**Reset coupling.** The async clear of both reset synchronizers is `wrst_n & rrst_n`, so
asserting either reset immediately (asynchronously) resets **both** pointer sets. Each side
leaves reset synchronously to its own clock, after both inputs are de-asserted.

## 7. Timing & Pipeline

- **Throughput:** one write per `wclk` and one read per `rclk`, sustained.
- **Write → visible to reader (empty de-assert):** the `wgray` register updates at write edge W0. `rq1` captures it at the first `rclk` edge after W0 (+setup), `rq2` at the next, and `rempty_q` at the third. Latency is 2–3 `rclk` cycles plus up to one `rclk` period of phase uncertainty, about 15–20 ns at 200 MHz.
- **Read → space visible to writer (full de-assert):** 2–3 `wclk` cycles plus phase, about 27–40 ns at 74.25 MHz.
- **Read data latency:** 1 `rclk` cycle after an accepted `rd_en`.
- **Sizing:** the reader (200 MHz) is faster than the writer (74.25 MHz), so in steady state the FIFO runs near empty. DEPTH = 32 absorbs reader stalls of up to 32 / 74.25 MHz ≈ 430 ns.

Cycle trace, read domain: a single write to an empty FIFO (`wgray` goes 000000 → 000001 at t = 0):

| rclk edge | `rq1_wgray` | `rq2_wgray` | `rempty_q` | `rd_en` | `rd_data_q` | `rd_valid` |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|------------|---------|-------------|------------|
| R0 (t ≈ 1 ns) | 000001 | 000000 | 1 | 0 | – | 0 |
| R1 | 000001 | 000001 | 1 | 0 | – | 0 |
| R2 | 000001 | 000001 | **0** | 1 | – | 0 |
| R3 | 000001 | 000001 | 1 | 0 | **D0** | 1 |

Each row shows register values after that edge; `rd_en` is the value driven in the following
cycle. The consumer sees `rd_empty=0` after R2 and raises `rd_en`, which is accepted at R3
(`r_fire=1`, `rbin_n=1`, `rgray_n=000001 == rq2_wgray`). At R3 `rd_data_q` captures D0
and `rempty_q` is set again.

Write domain: filling to full with no reads (DEPTH=32). After the 32nd accepted write,
`wbin = 32 = 100000b`, `wgray = 110000b`; `rgray = 000000` with its two MSBs inverted is
`110000` → `wr_full` = 1 in the same cycle the 32nd write is registered.

## 8. Clocking & Reset

**Clock domains:** `wclk` (74.25 MHz, may stop) and `rclk` (200 MHz), asynchronous.

**Crossings**

| # | Signal | From → To | Width | Method |
|---|--------|-----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | `wgray` | wclk → rclk | `PTR_W` | Gray code + `SYNC_STAGES`-FF synchronizer |
| 2 | `rgray` | rclk → wclk | `PTR_W` | Gray code + `SYNC_STAGES`-FF synchronizer |
| 3 | `mem[*]` → `rd_data_q` | wclk → rclk | `DATA_W` | Qualified by pointer protocol (entry stable ≥ 2 rclk before it can be read) |
| 4 | `wrst_n` → rclk logic, `rrst_n` → wclk logic | async | 1 | Reset synchronizers (async assert, sync de-assert) |

**Constraints (SDC/XDC)**

```tcl
set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group [get_clocks wclk] -group [get_clocks rclk]
# Gray buses: bound skew/delay to the *faster* (source-side worst) period so at most one bit is in flight
set_max_delay -datapath_only 5.000 -from [get_cells u_wptr/wgray_reg[*]] -to [get_cells u_sync_w2r/q1_reg[*]]
set_max_delay -datapath_only 5.000 -from [get_cells u_rptr/rgray_reg[*]] -to [get_cells u_sync_r2w/q1_reg[*]]
# Vivado alternative / addition:
set_bus_skew 5.000 -from [get_cells u_wptr/wgray_reg[*]] -to [get_cells u_sync_w2r/q1_reg[*]]
set_bus_skew 5.000 -from [get_cells u_rptr/rgray_reg[*]] -to [get_cells u_sync_r2w/q1_reg[*]]
# Memory read path is protocol-qualified; bound it to one rclk period
set_max_delay -datapath_only 5.000 -from [get_cells u_mem/mem_reg[*][*]] -to [get_cells u_rptr/rd_data_q_reg[*]]
set_property ASYNC_REG TRUE [get_cells {u_sync_*/q*_reg[*] u_*rst/s*_reg}]
```

**SpyGlass CDC setup:** declare `wclk`/`rclk` as asynchronous clock domains, and declare the
FIFO so that rule `Ac_unsync02` on the memory path is waived as FIFO-qualified:
`fifo -memory u_mem.mem -rd_ptr u_rptr.rbin -wr_ptr u_wptr.wbin`. The synchronizers are
recognized as conventional multi-flop (`Ac_sync01`); the Gray-encoded buses pass
`Ac_conv02`.

**Reset:** two async active-low resets. Either one asserted resets both sides (coupled
async clear); each side releases synchronously to its own clock. If `wclk` is stopped
when the resets de-assert, the write side stays in reset until `wclk` runs, which is
harmless: no writes can happen without a clock.

## 9. Corner Cases & Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| `wr_en` while `wr_full` | Ignored. Data not written. No error flag (spec does not ask for one). |
| `rd_en` while `rd_empty` | Ignored; `rd_data_q` holds; `rd_valid=0`. |
| `wclk` stops with data in FIFO | Reader still sees the last synchronized `wgray` and drains everything written. |
| `rclk` stops | Writer fills to full and then stops accepting; no loss. |
| Only one side reset | Coupled reset clears both sides; in-flight data is discarded (it is invalid anyway after a one-sided reset). |
| Synchronizer goes metastable | Resolves to old or new Gray value; both are valid pointers, so flags are at worst pessimistic for one more cycle. |
| `AF_LEVEL`/`AE_LEVEL` | Based on stale remote pointer: `almost_full` may be late to clear, `almost_empty` may be late to clear (both conservative). |
| Pointer wrap | `PTR_W`-bit modulo arithmetic; MSB distinguishes full/empty. |

## 10. Verification Plan

**Testbench:** two independent clock generators with randomized period jitter and random
start phase; ratios swept from 1:5 to 5:1 (not just 74.25/200). A scoreboard queue checks
ordering, no loss and no duplication. Writer and reader traffic generators have random
duty cycles.

**Directed tests**
1. Reset values: `rd_empty=1`, `wr_full=0`, `rd_almost_empty=1`.
2. Single write → measure empty de-assert latency (2–3 rclk).
3. Fill to full with the reader stalled; check exactly DEPTH words accepted.
4. Drain to empty; the extra `rd_en` is ignored.
5. Stop `wclk` mid-stream; the reader drains all accepted words.
6. Assert `wrst_n` alone mid-traffic → both sides empty; then resume.
7. Thresholds: `wr_almost_full` at level ≥ `AF_LEVEL`, `rd_almost_empty` at ≤ `AE_LEVEL`.

**Random:** 1M words with random clock ratios and traffic, including the extremes of a
reader 10× faster and a writer 10× faster.

**CDC-specific:** run with a metastability-injection model in the synchronizers (random
extra cycle of delay per bit) to prove the protocol tolerates it. Run SpyGlass CDC and RDC
with zero unwaived violations.

**Assertions (SVA)**

```systemverilog
a_wgray_onehot: assert property (@(posedge wclk) disable iff(!wrst_int_n) $onehot0(wgray ^ $past(wgray)));
a_rgray_onehot: assert property (@(posedge rclk) disable iff(!rrst_int_n) $onehot0(rgray ^ $past(rgray)));
a_no_wr_full:   assert property (@(posedge wclk) disable iff(!wrst_int_n) wfull_q |-> $stable(wbin));
a_no_rd_empty:  assert property (@(posedge rclk) disable iff(!rrst_int_n) rempty_q |-> $stable(rbin));
a_wlevel_max:   assert property (@(posedge wclk) disable iff(!wrst_int_n) (wbin - gray2bin(wq2_rgray)) <= DEPTH);
```

**Coverage:** full and empty reached; wrap of both pointers ≥ 3 times; simultaneous full and
read activity; clock ratio bins; one-sided resets on each side; `wclk` stop/start.

## 11. Assumptions & Open Questions

1. **Coupled resets.** The spec says resets "can come at different times". We assume either side may be reset at any time and that resetting one side must flush the whole FIFO. If the sensor side needs to be reset without disturbing data already queued, a reset handshake protocol is needed instead.
2. **No overflow/underflow flags.** The spec asks for none; writers and readers must respect `wr_full`/`rd_empty`.
3. **`rd_valid` added** as a convenience, so the consumer does not need to delay `rd_en` itself.
4. **2 synchronizer stages** are sufficient at 200 MHz / 74.25 MHz for typical MTBF on modern nodes. Use `SYNC_STAGES = 3` if the library's MTBF analysis requires it.
5. **Skew bound = 5 ns** (the faster clock period) is used for both Gray buses, which is conservative for the `wclk`-sourced bus.
6. **DEPTH = 32** is assumed sufficient for the reader's worst-case stall (≈ 430 ns). Confirm against the system interconnect latency.

Hi team,

For the new 10G MAC we need a CRC block that can sit on the receive and transmit data paths and
compute the Ethernet FCS on the fly. Some background and what we need:

The data path inside the MAC is 32 bits wide, using an AXI-Stream-like valid/ready handshake.
Byte 0 of a frame is in bits [7:0] of the first word, byte 1 in [15:8], and so on. Frames are
any length from 1 byte upward. On the last word of a frame we get a 4-bit byte-enable telling
us how many of the bytes are real; the valid bytes are always packed at the bottom, so you'll
only see 0001, 0011, 0111 or 1111 there. Every other word is always fully populated.

The CRC is the standard Ethernet one: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, register preset to all ones,
reflected in and out like the 802.3 spec, and the result inverted at the end. A good sanity
check is that the ASCII string "123456789" should produce 0xCBF43926.

We need to process a full word every clock with no bubbles between frames, because the MAC
streams back-to-back frames. When a frame ends, please give us the final 32-bit CRC with its
own valid/ready so the TX side can append it and the RX side can compare it. The block
shouldn't modify the data stream; it just watches it, so it can be used as a "tap".

Target clock is 312.5 MHz on an UltraScale+ part. We'd like to reuse the block on ASIC later.
Reset is synchronous active-low like the rest of the MAC.

If something is malformed (for example a weird byte-enable), flag it somehow, but don't hang.

Thanks!

# Micro-architecture: `crc32_stream`

## 1. Overview

`crc32_stream` computes the IEEE 802.3 (Ethernet FCS) CRC-32 over a stream of 32-bit words,
4 bytes per clock, with no bubbles between back-to-back frames. It watches a valid/ready
stream without modifying it and, at the end of each frame, emits the final CRC on its own
valid/ready result channel.

Key features:
- CRC-32/ISO-HDLC parameters: polynomial 0x04C11DB7 (reflected form 0xEDB88320), init 0xFFFFFFFF, reflected input and output, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF.
- Reflected (LSB-first) shift-register formulation, so no explicit bit reversal of data or result is needed.
- Four parallel next-state networks (8/16/24/32 data bits) for the partial last word, selected by the byte-enable.
- Frame-to-frame CRC register reload in the same cycle as the last beat, giving 100% throughput.
- One registered result slot; sticky error flag for illegal byte-enable patterns.

## 2. Interface

| Name | Dir | Width | Description |
|------|-----|-------|-------------|
| **Clock / reset** | | | |
| `clk` | in | 1 | 312.5 MHz data-path clock. |
| `rst_n` | in | 1 | Synchronous active-low reset. |
| **Input stream (tap)** | | | |
| `s_valid` | in | 1 | Beat valid. |
| `s_ready` | out | 1 | Beat accepted when `s_valid && s_ready`. |
| `s_data` | in | 32 | Data; byte *i* of the beat is `s_data[8i+7:8i]`, byte 0 first on the wire. |
| `s_keep` | in | 4 | Byte enables; must be `4'b1111` except on the last beat. |
| `s_last` | in | 1 | Last beat of the frame. |
| **Result channel** | | | |
| `m_crc_valid` | out | 1 | Final CRC available. |
| `m_crc_ready` | in | 1 | Consumer accepts result. |
| `m_crc` | out | 32 | Final CRC (already reflected and inverted). FCS byte order on the wire is `m_crc[7:0]` first. |
| **Status** | | | |
| `keep_err` | out | 1 | Sticky: an illegal `s_keep` pattern was seen. |
| `err_clr` | in | 1 | Pulse; clears `keep_err`. |

When used as a pure tap, `s_ready` is ANDed into the parent stream's ready by the
integrator. It only deasserts in the rare case described in §6.

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Legal range | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `POLY_REFL` | `32'hEDB88320` | any 32-bit | Reflected polynomial (bit-reversed 0x04C11DB7). |
| `INIT` | `32'hFFFFFFFF` | any 32-bit | CRC register preset at frame start. |
| `XOROUT` | `32'hFFFFFFFF` | any 32-bit | Final XOR. |
| `DATA_W` | 32 | fixed 32 | Data width (fixed in this version; see §11). |
| `KEEP_W` | `DATA_W/8` = 4 | derived | Byte-enable width. |

Changing `POLY_REFL`/`INIT`/`XOROUT` gives any reflected CRC-32 variant. Non-reflected
variants are out of scope (§11).

## 4. Block Diagram

```
 s_data[31:0] ------------------+----------------+----------------+----------------+
                                |                |                |                |
 crc_q[31:0] --+--------------->|                |                |                |
               |          +-----v-----+    +-----v-----+    +-----v-----+    +-----v-----+
               |          | crc_nxt8  |    | crc_nxt16 |    | crc_nxt24 |    | crc_nxt32 |
               |          | (d[7:0])  |    | (d[15:0]) |    | (d[23:0]) |    | (d[31:0]) |
               |          +-----+-----+    +-----+-----+    +-----+-----+    +-----+-----+
               |                |c8              |c16             |c24             |c32
               |                +-------+--------+-------+--------+-------+--------+
               |                        |   4:1 mux, sel = nbytes (from s_keep, s_last)
               |                        v
               |                   crc_upd[31:0] ----------------+
               |                        |                        | ^ XOROUT
               |        INIT --->|\     |                        v
               |                 | |<---+               +--------------+
               +-----------------| |  sel = s_last      |   res_q      |---> m_crc
                     crc_q <-----|/                     | res_valid_q  |---> m_crc_valid
                                                        +--------------+
 s_keep,s_last ---> keep decode ---> nbytes, keep_bad ---> keep_err_q (sticky)
```

| Instance | Module | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `u_nxt8/16/24/32` | `crc32_nxt #(.NBITS(8/16/24/32))` | Purely combinational XOR networks computing the CRC after N data bits. |
| — (inline) | keep decode | Maps `s_keep`/`s_last` to `nbytes` and `keep_bad`. |
| — (inline) | result slot | `res_q`, `res_valid_q`, output handshake. |

## 5. Datapath

**Registers**

| Register | Width | Reset | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|---------|
| `crc_q` | 32 | `INIT` | Running CRC of the current frame (reflected, not inverted). |
| `res_q` | 32 | 0 | Final CRC of the last completed frame. |
| `res_valid_q` | 1 | 0 | `res_q` holds an unconsumed result. |
| `keep_err_q` | 1 | 0 | Sticky illegal-keep flag. |

**Next-state networks.** Each `crc32_nxt` instance is the unrolled reflected LFSR. It is
written as a constant-bound loop that synthesis flattens into an XOR network (no registers):

```verilog
function automatic [31:0] crc_nxt(input [31:0] c, input [31:0] d, input integer nbits);
  integer i;
  begin
    crc_nxt = c;
    for (i = 0; i < nbits; i = i + 1)
      crc_nxt = (crc_nxt >> 1) ^ (((crc_nxt[0] ^ d[i]) ? POLY_REFL : 32'h0));
  end
endfunction
```

Data bit `d[0]` (the LSB of byte 0) is processed first, matching Ethernet's LSB-first bit
order. That is why the reflected form needs no bit reversal. For 32 data bits, each output
bit is the XOR of at most about 30 inputs (bits of `crc_q` and `s_data`). That maps to 2–3
LUT6 levels, comfortably within the 3.2 ns budget.

**Byte-count decode**

| `s_last` | `s_keep` | `nbytes` | `keep_bad` |
|----------|----------|----------|------------|
| 0 | `1111` | 4 | 0 |
| 0 | other | 4 | 1 |
| 1 | `0001` | 1 | 0 |
| 1 | `0011` | 2 | 0 |
| 1 | `0111` | 3 | 0 |
| 1 | `1111` | 4 | 0 |
| 1 | other non-zero | highest set bit index + 1 | 1 |
| 1 | `0000` | 0 (CRC unchanged) | 1 |

```verilog
crc_upd = (nbytes == 1) ? c8 : (nbytes == 2) ? c16 : (nbytes == 3) ? c24 :
          (nbytes == 4) ? c32 : crc_q;
```

**Register updates (when `s_fire = s_valid && s_ready`)**

```verilog
crc_q       <= s_last ? INIT : crc_upd;
if (s_last) begin
  res_q       <= crc_upd ^ XOROUT;
end
res_valid_q <= (s_fire && s_last) ? 1'b1 : (m_crc_ready ? 1'b0 : res_valid_q);
keep_err_q  <= err_clr ? 1'b0 : (keep_err_q | (s_fire && keep_bad));
```

## 6. Control Logic

There is no explicit FSM. Frame state is implicit: `crc_q == INIT` marks the start of a
frame, and `s_last` closes it. The only control is the result-slot handshake.

| Implied state | Condition | Behaviour |
|---------------|-----------|-----------|
| IN_FRAME | always | Every accepted beat updates `crc_q`; a last beat reloads `INIT`. |
| RESULT_EMPTY | `res_valid_q == 0` | Last beat may complete; `s_ready = 1`. |
| RESULT_PENDING | `res_valid_q == 1` | `m_crc_valid = 1`; a new last beat can only be accepted if `m_crc_ready` frees the slot in the same cycle. |

```verilog
assign s_ready     = !res_valid_q || m_crc_ready;
assign m_crc_valid = res_valid_q;
assign m_crc       = res_q;
```

`s_ready` is combinational from `m_crc_ready`. The consumer (MAC TX/RX control) reads the
result in the cycle it appears, so in normal operation `s_ready` stays at 1 and the data
path never stalls. If the result consumer must be fully decoupled, a register slice can be
put on the result channel (§11).

## 7. Timing & Pipeline

- **Latency:** the final CRC is valid one cycle after the last beat is accepted.
- **Throughput:** 32 bits per clock (10 Gb/s at 312.5 MHz), with back-to-back frames and no idle cycles, because `crc_q` reloads `INIT` in the same edge that captures the result.
- **Critical path:** `crc_q`/`s_data` → `crc_nxt32` XOR tree → 4:1 mux → `crc_q` D-input (about 4 LUT levels). `s_keep` decode runs in parallel with the XOR trees.

Cycle-by-cycle: frame A = "123456789" (9 bytes), immediately followed by frame B.
`m_crc_ready = 1` throughout.

| Cycle | s_valid | s_data | s_keep | s_last | crc_q (during) | res_valid | m_crc | Note |
|-------|---------|--------|--------|--------|----------------|-----------|-------|------|
| 0 | 1 | `34333231` | `1111` | 0 | `FFFFFFFF` | 0 | – | "1234" |
| 1 | 1 | `38373635` | `1111` | 0 | `641C1F5C` | 0 | – | "5678" |
| 2 | 1 | `xxxxxx39` | `0001` | 1 | `651F2550` | 0 | – | "9"; crc_upd = `340BC6D9` |
| 3 | 1 | B0 | `1111` | 0 | `FFFFFFFF` | 1 | `CBF43926` | frame B starts, A's result out |
| 4 | 1 | B1 | `1111` | 0 | f(B0) | 0 | – | |

## 8. Clocking & Reset

- Single clock domain `clk`; no CDC.
- `rst_n` is synchronous active-low. Reset loads `crc_q = INIT` and clears `res_valid_q` and `keep_err_q`. `res_q` is reset to 0 for clean waveforms; this costs 32 flops with reset, which is negligible.
- The block has no requirement on what happens to a frame interrupted by reset. Upstream must restart frames after reset.

## 9. Corner Cases & Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| 1-byte frame | Single beat with `s_last=1`, `s_keep=0001`: `crc_q` goes `INIT → INIT`, result = `crc_nxt8(INIT, d) ^ XOROUT`. |
| Back-to-back last beats (1-beat frames every cycle) | Supported at full rate as long as `m_crc_ready=1`; each result occupies the slot for one cycle. |
| Result not consumed, new last beat arrives | `s_ready=0`; the beat waits. Non-last beats also stall, because `s_ready` does not look at `s_last` (keeps the logic simple; §11). |
| Illegal keep on non-last beat | Treated as 4 bytes, `keep_err` set. |
| Non-contiguous keep on last beat (e.g. `0101`) | Byte count = highest set bit + 1 (here 3), `keep_err` set. |
| `s_keep = 0000` with `s_last` | Frame closes with CRC unchanged by this beat, `keep_err` set. |
| `s_valid` low mid-frame | `crc_q` holds; gaps are allowed anywhere. |
| `err_clr` and new error in the same cycle | `err_clr` wins (clear has priority). |

## 10. Verification Plan

**Reference model:** a bytewise reflected CRC-32 (equal to Python `zlib.crc32` / C `crc32()`),
fed from the same byte stream as the DUT.

**Directed tests**
1. "123456789" as 3 beats (keep `1111`,`1111`,`0001`) → `0xCBF43926`, with the intermediate `crc_q` values listed in §7.
2. Every last-beat keep (`0001`,`0011`,`0111`,`1111`) for frame lengths 1–12.
3. Minimum-size (64-byte) and jumbo (9000-byte) Ethernet frames, plus real captured frames with known FCS.
4. Residue check: running the CRC over a frame *plus* its appended FCS must give a constant register value for every frame. The value is computed by the reference model and compared, not hard-coded.
5. Back-to-back 1-beat frames for 100 cycles with `m_crc_ready=1` → one result per cycle.
6. Result back-pressure: hold `m_crc_ready=0` and check that `s_ready` falls only while a result is pending.
7. Illegal keep patterns → `keep_err` sticky and cleared by `err_clr`.

**Constrained-random:** random frame lengths 1–2000 bytes, random `s_valid` gaps, random
`m_crc_ready` (90% high), 1M beats; scoreboard compares every result.

**Assertions (SVA)**

```systemverilog
a_res_stable: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n)
                m_crc_valid && !m_crc_ready |=> m_crc_valid && $stable(m_crc));
a_init_after_last: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n)
                s_valid && s_ready && s_last |=> crc_q == INIT);
a_ready_hi: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n) !m_crc_valid |-> s_ready);
a_keep_full: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(!rst_n)
                s_valid && !s_last |-> s_keep == 4'hF);   // warning-level, environment check
```

**Coverage:** each `nbytes` value on the last beat; 1-beat frames; gap mid-frame; result
back-pressure; `keep_err` set and clear; back-to-back frames with no idle cycle.

**Equivalence:** formally check the unrolled `crc32_nxt` instances against 8/16/24/32
iterations of the serial LFSR (SymbiYosys or a commercial LEC).

## 11. Assumptions & Open Questions

1. **Reflected implementation only.** The spec asks for 802.3, which is reflected in and out. Supporting `REFIN=0` variants would need bit reversal per byte and is left out.
2. **`DATA_W` fixed at 32.** A 64-bit variant (for a future 25G path) needs 8 networks; the function above generalizes, but the keep decode and timing would need review.
3. **`s_ready` does not look at `s_last`.** Stalling only last beats would need `s_ready` to depend combinationally on `s_last`. Because the consumer always reads the result immediately, the simpler rule is used.
4. **Error reporting** is a sticky flag only; the frame's CRC is still produced so downstream can drop it. Confirm whether an in-band error bit on the result channel is wanted.
5. **Result ordering on the wire.** `m_crc[7:0]` is the first FCS byte transmitted. The TX inserter must not byte-swap.
6. **Synchronous reset** chosen to match the MAC. On ASIC, the result and CRC registers may drop reset if area matters.

# Micro-architecture: `fxp_mac`

## 1. Overview

`fxp_mac` is a pipelined signed fixed-point multiply-accumulate unit. Each valid input pair
`(a, b)` is multiplied and added to a full-precision accumulator. A running, rounded,
saturated result is emitted for every valid input. `in_clr` starts a new sum with the
current product, so back-to-back accumulations have no dead cycle.

Key features:
- Parameterized operand, accumulator and output widths; default Q1.15 × Q1.15 → Q10.30 accumulator (40 bits) → Q1.15 output.
- Three arithmetic register stages (input, multiply, accumulate) that map one-to-one onto DSP48E2 `AREG/BREG`, `MREG` and `PREG`, plus one fabric stage for saturation. Total latency is 4 cycles.
- Round-to-nearest (ties toward +∞) at zero cost, by pre-loading the rounding bias into the accumulator on clear.
- Output saturation with a per-sample `out_sat` flag; sticky accumulator-overflow flag.
- Valid-only pipeline (no back-pressure) with a `last` sideband matched in latency.

## 2. Interface

| Name | Dir | Width | Description |
|------|-----|-------|-------------|
| **Clock / reset** | | | |
| `clk` | in | 1 | 400 MHz clock. |
| `rst` | in | 1 | Synchronous active-high reset. |
| **Input** | | | |
| `in_valid` | in | 1 | `in_a`/`in_b`/`in_clr`/`in_last` are valid. |
| `in_a` | in | `A_W` | Signed operand a (two's complement, `A_FRAC` fractional bits). |
| `in_b` | in | `B_W` | Signed operand b (`B_FRAC` fractional bits). |
| `in_clr` | in | 1 | This sample starts a new accumulation (acc = a·b instead of acc + a·b). |
| `in_last` | in | 1 | Sideband; delayed to `out_last`. |
| **Output** | | | |
| `out_valid` | out | 1 | `out_y` holds the result for one input sample. |
| `out_y` | out | `OUT_W` | Rounded, saturated running sum (`OUT_FRAC` fractional bits). |
| `out_sat` | out | 1 | `out_y` was saturated for this sample. |
| `out_last` | out | 1 | `in_last` of the corresponding sample. |
| `out_acc` | out | `ACC_W` | Full-precision accumulator (debug/chaining), includes rounding bias (§5). |
| **Status** | | | |
| `acc_ovf` | out | 1 | Sticky: the accumulator wrapped. |
| `err_clr` | in | 1 | Clears `acc_ovf`. |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Legal range | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
| `A_W` | 16 | 2–27 | Width of a (≤27 for a single DSP48E2 A port). |
| `B_W` | 16 | 2–18 | Width of b (≤18 for the B port). |
| `A_FRAC` | 15 | 0..`A_W-1` | Fractional bits of a. |
| `B_FRAC` | 15 | 0..`B_W-1` | Fractional bits of b. |
| `ACC_W` | 40 | `A_W+B_W`–48 | Accumulator width (≤48 for the DSP P register). |
| `OUT_W` | 16 | 2..`ACC_W` | Output width. |
| `OUT_FRAC` | 15 | ≤ `A_FRAC+B_FRAC` | Output fractional bits. |
| `P_W` | `A_W+B_W` | derived | Product width (32). |
| `SHIFT` | `A_FRAC+B_FRAC-OUT_FRAC` | derived | Output right-shift (15). |
| `GUARD` | `ACC_W-P_W` | derived | Guard bits (8). |
| `RND` | `SHIFT>0 ? 1<<(SHIFT-1) : 0` | derived | Rounding bias (`0x4000`). |

**Guard-bit check.** The largest-magnitude product is (−1)·(−1) = +2^30 in Q2.30 (fits in
32 signed bits). A 40-bit accumulator holds up to 2^39 − 1, so 2^39/2^30 = 512 full-scale
products can be summed without overflow. That meets the "≥256" requirement. An elaboration
check `$error`s if `ACC_W < P_W + 8`.

in_clr -->[c1]--------->[c2]
in_last ->[l1]--------->[l2]------------------------->[l3]------------------------->[l4]---> out_last

| Instance | Module | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `u_dsp` | inferred (or `DSP48E2` primitive) | S1–S3: input regs, multiplier, accumulator with W-mux selecting `RND` (C port) or P feedback. |
| — (inline) | `sat_round` | S4: arithmetic shift and saturation in fabric. |
| — (inline) | valid/sideband pipe | 4-deep shift registers for `valid`, `last`; 2-deep for `clr`. |

## 5. Datapath

**Registers**

| Register | Width | Reset | Stage | Purpose |
|----------|-------|-------|-------|---------|
| `a1_q`, `b1_q` | `A_W`, `B_W` | 0 | S1 | Input operands (DSP AREG/BREG). |
| `v1_q`, `c1_q`, `l1_q` | 1 each | 0 | S1 | valid / clr / last. |
| `p2_q` | `P_W` | 0 | S2 | Product `a1_q * b1_q` (signed; DSP MREG). |
| `v2_q`, `c2_q`, `l2_q` | 1 each | 0 | S2 | |
| `acc_q` | `ACC_W` | `RND` | S3 | Accumulator (DSP PREG). |
| `v3_q`, `l3_q` | 1 each | 0 | S3 | |
| `y4_q` | `OUT_W` | 0 | S4 | Saturated output. |
| `sat4_q`, `v4_q`, `l4_q` | 1 each | 0 | S4 | |
| `acc_ovf_q` | 1 | 0 | – | Sticky overflow. |

The S1 and S2 data registers (`a1_q`, `b1_q`, `p2_q`) advance every cycle regardless of
valid, which keeps them DSP-friendly (no CE needed). Only `acc_q` is qualified by `v2_q`.

**Multiply (S2):** `p2_q <= $signed(a1_q) * $signed(b1_q)`. `p_ext` is `p2_q` sign-extended
to `ACC_W`.

**Accumulate (S3) with rounding bias**

```verilog
if (v2_q)
  acc_q <= c2_q ? (p_ext + RND) : (acc_q + p_ext);
```

Adding `RND` once at the start of each sum means `acc_q >>> SHIFT` (floor) equals
round-to-nearest of the true sum. No rounding adder is needed in S4. The reset value of
`acc_q` is also `RND`, so a sum started without `in_clr` after reset is rounded correctly
too. On the DSP48E2, `C = RND` and `OPMODE` selects `W = C` when `c2_q`, else `W = P`.

**Overflow detect (S3):** only in the accumulate case (`!c2_q`). If `acc_q` and `p_ext`
have the same sign and the sum's sign differs, set `acc_ovf_q`. (The clear case cannot
overflow because `|p_ext + RND| < 2^(ACC_W-1)`.)

**Saturate (S4)**

```verilog
wire signed [ACC_W-SHIFT-1:0] r = acc_q >>> SHIFT;            // rounded value
wire hi  = (r >  $signed({1'b0, {(OUT_W-1){1'b1}}}));         // > MAX
wire lo  = (r <  $signed({1'b1, {(OUT_W-1){1'b0}}}));         // < MIN
y4_q   <= hi ? {1'b0,{(OUT_W-1){1'b1}}} : lo ? {1'b1,{(OUT_W-1){1'b0}}} : r[OUT_W-1:0];
sat4_q <= v3_q & (hi | lo);
```

In hardware, `hi`/`lo` reduce to "bits `r[ACC_W-SHIFT-1:OUT_W-1]` are not all equal",
with the sign bit picking the direction. That is a 10-bit AND/OR reduction (2 LUT levels).

## 6. Control Logic

There is no FSM; control is entirely the valid/sideband pipe.

| Signal | Equation |
|--------|----------|
| `v1_q, c1_q, l1_q` | `<= in_valid, in_valid & in_clr, in_last` |
| `v2_q, c2_q, l2_q` | `<= v1_q, c1_q, l1_q` |
| `acc_en` | `v2_q` (DSP `CEP`) |
| `acc_sel_rnd` | `c2_q` (DSP `OPMODE[W]` = C vs P) |
| `v3_q, l3_q` | `<= v2_q, l2_q` |
| `v4_q, l4_q` | `<= v3_q, l3_q` |
| `out_valid, out_last` | `= v4_q, l4_q & v4_q` |
| `acc_ovf_q` | `<= err_clr ? 0 : acc_ovf_q \| (v2_q & !c2_q & ovf)` |

`in_clr` is masked with `in_valid`, so a stray clear on an invalid cycle has no effect.

## 7. Timing & Pipeline

- **Latency:** 4 cycles from `in_valid` to `out_valid` (S1, S2, S3, S4).
- **Throughput:** 1 MAC per clock; clear costs no extra cycle.
- **Critical paths at 400 MHz (2.5 ns):** multiplier and 48-bit ALU are inside the hard DSP pipeline; the fabric path is `acc_q` (PREG) → shift (wiring) → 10-bit saturation reduction → output mux → `y4_q`, about 3 LUT levels.

| Cyc | in (a, b, clr) | p2_q (S2) | acc_q (S3, during) | out_y (S4) | out_sat | Note |

## 8. Clocking & Reset

- Single clock `clk`; no CDC.
- `rst` is synchronous active-high, matching DSP48E2 `RSTx` pins (which are synchronous). Valid/sideband flops and `acc_ovf_q` must be reset. Data registers are reset for determinism, but the reset can be removed from `a1_q`/`b1_q`/`p2_q` if routing congestion matters, because `out_valid` qualifies everything.
- `acc_q` resets to `RND`, not 0 (see §5).

## 9. Corner Cases & Error Handling

| Case | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|
| (−1) × (−1) | Product +1.0 (`0x4000_0000`), representable in Q2.30; output saturates to `0x7FFF` (+0.99997), `out_sat=1`. |
| Ties in rounding | x.5 LSB rounds toward +∞ (e.g. −0.5 LSB → 0). This is documented; convergent rounding is an open option (§11). |
| More than 512 full-scale products | Accumulator wraps, `acc_ovf` sets (sticky); outputs are wrong until the next `in_clr`. |
| Saturation is not sticky | The accumulator keeps full precision; the output recovers once the sum is back in range. |
| `in_clr` on an invalid cycle | Ignored (masked with `in_valid`). |
| Gaps in `in_valid` | `acc_q` holds; output only on valid samples. |
| `SHIFT = 0` | `RND = 0`; no rounding needed. |

## 10. Verification Plan

**Reference model:** an arbitrary-precision integer model computing `sum = Σ a·b` per
accumulation, `y = clamp(floor((sum + RND) / 2^SHIFT))`, plus the overflow flag from a
wrapped `ACC_W`-bit sum.

**Directed tests**
1. The §7 sequence: exact values and `out_sat`.
2. Corner operands: all combinations of {MIN, −1 LSB, 0, +1 LSB, MAX}².
3. Rounding ties: products giving exactly ±0.5 LSB of output.
4. Positive and negative saturation, then recovery without `in_clr`.
5. 512 products of (−1)(−1): no overflow; the 513th sets `acc_ovf`.
6. Back-to-back clears (each sample a 1-element sum).
7. Valid gaps between accumulating samples.
8. Parameter sets: (16,16,40,16), (18,25,48,24), (8,8,24,8).

**Random:** 1M random samples with random `in_clr` (5%), random valid duty cycle; scoreboard
on `out_y`, `out_sat`, `out_last`.

**Assertions**

```systemverilog
a_latency: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(rst) in_valid |-> ##4 out_valid);
a_novalid: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(rst) !in_valid |-> ##4 !out_valid);
a_sat_rng: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(rst)
             out_valid && !out_sat |-> ($signed($past(out_acc)) >>> SHIFT) == $signed(out_y));
// out_y (S4) lags acc_q (S3) by one cycle, hence $past.
a_ovf_sticky: assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff(rst) acc_ovf && !err_clr |=> acc_ovf);
```

**Implementation check:** post-synthesis utilization shows exactly 1 DSP48E2 and no fabric
multipliers. Timing passes at 400 MHz.

## 11. Assumptions & Open Questions

1. **"~3 stages" vs. saturation.** The three arithmetic stages map onto the DSP. Saturation needs a fabric stage, giving 4 cycles total latency. Folding saturation into S3 would put a 40-bit add plus compare in one cycle and break the DSP mapping, so the extra cycle is the deliberate choice.
2. **Rounding mode** is round-half-up (ties toward +∞), implemented via the bias pre-load. If symmetric or convergent rounding is required, S4 needs the discarded bits and an extra adder.
3. **Output each cycle** is interpreted as "every valid sample produces the running sum". A dot-product-only output (valid only on `last`) can be obtained by the consumer gating with `out_last`.
4. **Accumulator wrap is not saturated**, only flagged. The DSP ALU cannot saturate natively, and 8 guard bits exceed the stated requirement.
5. **No back-pressure**, as stated. If a downstream stall appears later, add a global CE to all stages (DSP CE pins) rather than a skid buffer.
6. `out_acc` includes the `RND` bias. Consumers that chain accumulators must subtract it or use `out_y`.
